title: Forms basics
summary: Collect text, email and passwords with form, input, label and button.

quiz.q: Which input type hides what the user types?
quiz.explain: `type="password"` shows dots instead of the characters. (`hidden` is an invisible field, not a masked one.)

quiz.q: Connect the label to the input.
quiz.explain: The label's `for` must match the input's `id`.

quiz.q: An input has no `name` attribute. What happens when the form is submitted?
options: The browser guesses a name from the id
quiz.explain: Only inputs with a `name` are included in the data that is sent. The `id` is for labels and styling.

quiz.q: Click the line with the mistake.
quiz.code:
<form action="/login" method="post">
  <label for="user">User</label>
  <input id="username" name="user" type="text">
  <button type="submit">Log in</button>
</form>
quiz.explain: The label points to `user` but the input's id is `username`, so they are not connected. Make them match.

exercise.task:
Build a registration form in `index.html`.

- A `<form>` with `action="/register"` and `method="post"`.
- A text input with `id="name"` and `name="name"`, with a label that has `for="name"` and the text `Name`.
- An email input with `id="email"` and `name="email"`, with a matching label `Email`.
- A password input (`type="password"`) with `name="password"`.
- A submit button that says `Register`.
hints: Start with the form element and its two attributes, then add the fields one at a time.
Each label needs for="x" and the input needs id="x". The input type is what makes it text, email or password.

<form action="/register" method="post">
  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" name="name" type="text">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email">
  <input name="password" type="password">
  <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>

checks.name: A text input has id and name "name"
An email input has id and name "email"
checks.hint: Use type="email" with id="email" and name="email".
